title: Which comes first, dry bottom or spill? 4 cm of water: dry at 342 rpm. 6 cm: spills at 342 rpm
description:
A glass of water, spun up. Which comes first, dry bottom or spill? Two panels, side view in cross-section, the same straight-sided glass: inner radius 3.5 cm (7 cm across), 10 cm tall, on a turntable platter. Top panel 4 cm of water (153.9 mL), bottom panel 6 cm (230.9 mL). Both are spun up on the same ramp: at rest until 3 s, then 15 rpm per second up to 450 rpm at 33 s, held to the end at 40 s. The water turns with the glass as one body (rigid rotation, the quasi-steady state after spin-up; real water lags a glass that is spun up quickly, which is why the ramp is slow), so its surface is the paraboloid z = z0 + w^2 r^2 / (2 g) with the depth from rim to centre d = w^2 R^2 / (2 g), g = 9.807 m/s^2. While the bottom is covered and nothing has spilled the mean level is the fill: centre h - d / 2, rim h + d / 2. Past the dry point the water is a ring with z = (w^2 / (2 g)) (r^2 - r0^2); past the spill point the rim stays at 10 cm and the volume shrinks to the most the glass can hold at that speed. Every state is a closed form of the speed alone; nothing is integrated. Deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- 4 cm of water: the bottom shows first, at 35.790 rad/s = 341.8 rpm (closed form sqrt(4 g h) / R), the rim then at 8.0 cm (the dip of 4.0 cm equals the climb of 4.0 cm), nothing spilled; the dry disc grows and the rim reaches 10 cm only at 427.2 rpm, the dry radius then 1.57 cm; at 450 rpm 138.7 mL remain and 15.2 mL have spilled
- 6 cm of water: it spills first, at the same 341.8 rpm (closed form sqrt(4 g (H - h)) / R), the centre then 2.0 cm deep; from then the rim stays at 10 cm and the water leaves; the bottom shows at 40.014 rad/s = 382.1 rpm (closed form sqrt(2 g H) / R), when 192.4 mL of 230.9 mL remain (exactly half the glass) and 38.5 mL have spilled; at 450 rpm 138.7 mL remain, 92.2 mL spilled
- the wrong guess: sqrt(4 g h) / R with h = 6 cm gives 418.6 rpm for the bottom to show; it ignores the spilled water (it would put the rim at 12.0 cm, above the 10 cm glass); with the spill the bottom has been dry since 382.1 rpm
- half full (5 cm, 192.4 mL) is the swap: the bottom shows and the rim reaches 10 cm at the same 382.1 rpm; under half full the bottom shows first, over half full it spills first
- above 427.2 rpm both glasses hold the same water, pi g H^2 / w^2: 138.7 mL each at 450 rpm
- heights (centre, rim): 100 rpm: 4 cm glass 3.7 and 4.3 cm, 6 cm glass 5.7 and 6.3 cm; 200 rpm: 2.6 and 5.4, 4.6 and 7.4; 300 rpm: 0.9 and 7.1, 2.9 and 9.1; 400 rpm: 4 cm glass dry to 1.34 cm from the axis with the rim at 9.4 cm, 6 cm glass dry to 1.04 cm with the rim at 10.0 cm and 175.6 mL left
- a wider glass, 9 cm across (R 4.5 cm), with 4 cm: bottom dry at 265.8 rpm, spills at 332.3 rpm; the 7 cm glass with 2 cm (77.0 mL): dry at 241.7 rpm, spills at 604.2 rpm
- the schedule: 341.8 rpm at 25.78 s of video, 382.1 at 28.47 s, 427.2 at 31.48 s
- checks: the events found by bisection on the state agree with the closed forms (differences at most 1.5e-10 rad/s); the volume under the surface by Simpson quadrature agrees with the closed-form volume within 1e-6 L at every tabulated speed (worst 2.71e-14 mL); the water volume is monotone non-increasing over 4501 samples of the ramp; 19 of 21 brief figures agree at the brief's precision and 21 of 21 within one unit of its last digit (604.1 against the exact 604.2; 25.79 s against the exact 25.78 s)
- spin-up note (not drawn): water spun up suddenly takes about h / sqrt(nu w) to catch up with the glass (Ekman spin-up, nu = 1e-06 m^2/s): 6.7 s for 4 cm and 10.0 s for 6 cm at 341.8 rpm, so the 30 s ramp is slow against it

Why: the spin throws the water outward and up the wall, and the surface dips in the middle exactly as much as it climbs at the rim (the paraboloid's mean level is the fill while nothing spills). At 341.8 rpm the dip is 4 cm: in the 4 cm glass that empties the centre, while in the 6 cm glass the 4 cm climb has already taken the rim to 10 cm. Which comes first depends only on whether the fill is under or over half the glass: under half full the centre empties before the rim fills, over half full the rim fills first, and at exactly half full both happen at once, at 382.1 rpm. Once the deep glass spills, its rim is pinned at 10 cm and its bottom bares at 382.1 rpm, earlier than the 418.6 rpm you get by ignoring the spilled water.

Rerun sims/spinglass/spinglass.py with projects/spinglass/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.
